steps.caption: DeepBA, from a cold start
steps.say: A small network nudges them, step after step, until a ring of cameras stands around the scene.

scenes.headline: Bundle adjustment from a cold start
scenes.sub: DeepBA and TFD-SfM, and a video model that does geometry
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lambda. Two papers from one lab take away bundle adjustment's two crutches: the good first guess, and the point tracks.

legend: Each residual touches one camera and one point
Each point block inverts on its own
Fold the points into the camera block
Solve for the cameras, then each point

steps.say: Bundle adjustment moves every camera and every point to fit the pixels. Its normal matrix is shaped like an arrow.
steps.term: Bundle adjustment: fit all cameras and points at once

steps.say: Each point only talks to itself, so its little block is cheap to invert.
Eliminate the points first. What's left is a system in the cameras alone.
Solve that, then recover each point on its own. That's every serious solver, and it needs to start close.

scenes.title: Toy, 90° turn, runs that converge
scenes.say: In my flatland toy, with a walk that turns ninety degrees, a start five degrees off reaches the minimum in all twenty scenes. A cold start, in six.

steps.say: TFD-SfM drops the shared point. Each side of a match gets its own Gaussian, with its own variance.
steps.term: Gaussian landmark: a point with its own spread

steps.caption: A bad match grows its variance and stops pulling
steps.say: A match that can't be fitted grows its variance and stops pulling. As the ring resolves, the two discs merge.
From identity cameras, classical bundle adjustment gets almost nothing right on ETH3D.
Gaussian landmarks alone lift it to forty-five.
Chaining each pose to its parent in a spanning tree adds about thirty points.
Down-weighting unreliable image pairs takes it to ninety.
Object scans have a mirror trap: the reflected shape projects almost the same. So it optimises both worlds and keeps the likelier one.
DeepBA keeps that state, poses and depth maps, and replaces the solver with a graph network that predicts each update.

steps.caption: 2.04M parameters, the same weights every step
steps.say: Cameras, image pairs and matches pass messages. It sees residuals, never pixels, which is why two million parameters are enough.

scenes.title: RTA at 5°, the two papers' tables
scenes.say: Side by side, the optimiser wins the big scenes, and the network wins small bags of tourist photos. The protocols differ, so read it as a map.

steps.caption: 292 images: 56 s against 988 s
steps.say: And it's fast. On two hundred ninety-two images, its solver takes fifty-six seconds. COLMAP's takes nine hundred eighty-eight.
UGG comes from the other side: a video model that also generates depth and camera rays, fourteen point eight billion parameters of it.

steps.caption: No VGGT or COLMAP in its pose tables
steps.say: Its pose tables leave out the models people actually use.

scenes.text: Learned cold start, classical finish. DeepBA plus a real bundle adjustment is the pipeline to want.
scenes.say: A learned cold start, then a classical finish. DeepBA's own ablation says so. Neither paper has released code yet.

recap: Both pinhole only, no code yet
